content.thinking:
I need to understand how canceled project cards are counted as open.

getProjectStats must count both done and canceled as closed. The overdue query should exclude closed statuses and only flag open, non-archived issues past their due time. Reopening an issue must clear its completion date by checking terminal statuses. The sweep logic correctly excludes canceled issues from overdue counts.

The overdue job should list all non-deleted organizations instead of relying on listOrgIdsForRollup, which misses new workspaces and includes deleted ones. Once an issue is announced, it will never be announced again, even if it later becomes overdue again.

The sweep should track a current overdue set. After each run, it should emit only issues newly overdue and update the reported set to match exactly. This lets previously reported issues be re-announced once they become overdue again. The job iterates organization by organization, so batch limits might prevent it from seeing every workspace.

Scanning every organization each pass lets the reported set be replaced entirely with the union of overdue IDs found. This avoids dropping issues from organizations skipped by batch limits. Failed emits still need handling.

Failed emits will not be added to the reported set, so the next sweep retries them. The algorithm collects every issue still overdue into a `stillOverdue` set. It emits only newly overdue issues and adds them to the reported set. Afterward it removes any IDs from the reported set that are no longer overdue. This keeps the tracking set accurate across batches.

The alert workspace issue likely stems from an incorrect orgPredicate.

Checking orgPredicate. The completedAt timestamp resets on every close, which is fine if reopening clears it first. Still deciding whether terminal status transitions should preserve or reset that timestamp.

The fix is to set completedAt to the current stamp whenever entering a terminal status, and clear it when moving from a terminal to a non-terminal. The existing else branch incorrectly preserves the old timestamp.

The overdue job comment requires calling `emit` and `shouldFilterArchived` directly rather than reimplementing them.

The overdue job will use a new `listLiveOrgIds` repository function instead of `usageRepo.listOrgIdsForRollup`. This correctly includes brand-new workspaces and excludes deleted orgs that still have usage rows.

The 50-org batch limit will be removed so every live workspace is covered. The overdue issues query will also exclude closed statuses.

Drizzle's `notInArray` will filter out closed statuses in both overdue issue queries and project stats. Open counts will use `inArray` for done or canceled statuses. The optimistic reducer already clears `completedAt`. The due-time comparison uses strict less-than. Notification kind changes to `issue_overdue`.
insertNotifications uses the function argument orgId instead of input.orgId.

Adding a `listLiveOrgIds` method to the organization repository.

The overdue job will use a `seenOverdue` Set to track issues across organization loops. It will skip issues with null `dueAt` values and avoid duplicate reporting.

Failed emissions are retried on the next sweep. Issues that become overdue again will be announced. The query uses strict less-than for due dates and excludes closed statuses.
